notes: • Korea travel access: the map now owns the screen — Reach controls start collapsed behind a single toggle, legends stay clear of the bottom navigation pills, the Reach overlay is visible on phones, and the trip calendar opens on the current month. A misleading hand-drawn map legend was removed.

• Maps: smoother map behavior everywhere — tapping before a map has finished loading no longer errors, layer data updates in place without flicker, remote map data is cached for the session, and expanded cluster points no longer go stale after filtering.
• Sharing: when an edit is blocked by a project's access rules, the app now shows a clear message explaining the denial instead of failing silently.
• Website: the landing page gained About and FAQ pages.

• Korea travel access: the "Best spots" ranking can now be seen on the map. Tap a ranked district and press "Show on map" to open the map centred on it, or "See all 25 on the map" to compare the whole ranking at once as districts colored by the same tier colors as the list. The map carries its own floating "List" and "Show all 25" buttons, so you can flip between the two views without losing your place.

• Korea travel access: the "Best spots" ranking can now be seen on the map. Tap a ranked district and press "Show on map" to open the map centred on it, or "See all 25 on the map" to compare the whole ranking at once as districts colored by the same tier colors as the list. The map carries its own floating "Ranked list" and "Show all 25" buttons, so you can flip between the two views without losing your place.

• Korea travel access: Travel access now renders as a true heat map — the Reach Explorer's Heat toggle is a real continuously-blended gradient (no more grid-cell edges), maps now stay locked to north (no more accidental rotate/tilt), and panning the map no longer scrolls the page underneath it.

• Dispatch (new): set project rules right in the app — a group row's own Rules panel now has an editable rulesActive/rulesVersion/rules record editor (was API-only), with Recompute rules right alongside to refresh inheritance after you save.

• Dispatch (new): a project's overview gained a Plan chip — goals, milestones and decisions for that project, grouped and scoped to just its own subtree (previously a separate whole-board Plan tab). Project files gained a "Generate spec" action, and How dispatch works moved to the app's ⋮ menu.

• Dispatch (new): a project's overview gained a Plan chip — goals, milestones and decisions for that project, grouped and scoped to just its own subtree (previously a separate whole-board Plan tab). Project files gained a "Generate spec" action, and How dispatch works moved to the app's ⋮ menu.

• Korea travel access: the Reach Explorer is more compact on phone — the 8-hub picker is now a single row of tappable chips (swipe to switch hubs too), and the tier legend collapses under the map behind a "Reach tiers" tap-to-expand toggle, so the map itself gets much more of the screen.

• Korea travel access: the Reach Explorer's Buckets/Heat toggle — a continuous blue-to-gray access-time gradient, not just 8 flat tiers — now works on all 8 origin hubs (Seoul Station, City Hall, Gangnam, Wangsimni, Sadang, Jamsil, Konkuk, Hongik), previously only on Seoul Station.

• Dispatch: redesigned the Add-filter menu — tap-to-select checklists for status/lane/tag columns, a simple "contains…" field for text, plain range fields for numbers and dates, and a "Filters:" chip row with a ✕ per chip and a Clear all. Save a combination as a preset and reopen it in one tap.
• Dispatch: tap an empty area of a list to clear the current selection.
• Dispatch: fixed choppy scrolling in an embedded Priorities view (like a project's detail pane) — it now scrolls smoothly with the rest of the page instead of fighting its own inner scrollbar.

• Fixed a bug where "Dispatch (new)" could show a project as unshared — no members, invites rejected — even though the original Dispatch already had it shared, because the two looked up shares under different internal ids.
